title: What Happens When Everyone Has An AI Agent?
summary: What Happens When Everyone Has An AI Agent? ca.finance.yahoo.com
body:
David Morel, Contributor

Tue, September 1, 2026 at 3:01 a.m. PDT 4 min read

[](https://s.yimg.com/lo/mysterio/api/9ffb0c9602931febd5398813b8997f513c7685bea000b3f0f14eb736b64866ef/lightyear_networkapi/resizefit_w960%3Bquality_80%3Bformat_webp/https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.zenfs.com%2Fen%2Fforbes_contributor_845%2F63348490b5d5eb0364ab8bf0df011582.jpg)

Man standing in front of a screen presenting to colleagues

There's one thing no C-suite executive can escape in 2026 - an inbox full to the brim with pitches about what AI can do for their business. As the leader of a recruitment company, the onslaught feels particularly aggressive. There are tools that promise to find the best candidates in seconds, and 'agents' that can do the job of a whole team of consultants without the cost and people-management headaches. In a competitive market, it's easy to see why businesses succumb to the temptation of these grand claims because they promise speed, efficiency and reduced costs.

Agentic AI is simply the latest iteration of this rush to adoption, and I see businesses all around me fall victim to a fear of missing out on the latest thing. Unlike traditional chatbots and other simple AI tools, AI agents can take instructions, make decisions and execute actions, hence the heavy sales patter that they can replace human employees. To use recruitment as an example, an agent could select a shortlist, set up interviews with candidates and even host an initial screening call. The global AI agents market is valued at a massive 10.9 billion and is projected to expand rapidly into the early 2030s.

The question is, when every business invests in AI agents, how do they differentiate from one another? Tiger Recruitment is a values-driven business, and while we see the benefits of using AI in the right place, we are not about to hand over every selection decision to an agent. Like many businesses, we have drawn up a protocol for how AI should be used in the business that focuses on how the technology can augment the skills and experience of our consultants, rather than replace it. An AI agent does not see the personality of a perfect candidate - this is where the human touch adds value. Although an AI tool can remove bias and speed up certain aspects of the hiring process, it can't beat human client relationships where consultants instinctively know who is likely to be the right fit.

Bill Gates recently penned a 6,000-word essay extolling the virtues of human judgment in a world dominated by AI. The Microsoft co-founder argued for the creation of 'human-reserved' roles that cannot be replaced by technology, in areas where the skills required are 'irreplaceably human', such as caregiving. It's easy for business leaders to feel like they're falling behind when their competitors are announcing the latest AI-powered innovation, and it takes courage to step back and remain calm amid all the noise. A number of consulting businesses are also building cultures around in-person collaboration for more junior workers so they can develop the human skills so vital in the age of AI.
